questions.stem: Which OS image does the supplied CLZ-190 VM declaration use?

options.C: A custom image from Key Vault.
options.D: Windows Server 2022 Datacenter Azure Edition.

optionExplanations.A: That is not the configured Windows image.
optionExplanations.B: The lesson uses a Windows Server image.
optionExplanations.C: Key Vault is not an image repository and is not used here.
optionExplanations.D: The sku is 2022-datacenter-azure-edition.

sources.title: Create a Windows VM using Azure CLI

questions.stem: How does the Windows VM join the web subnet?

options.A: Through its network interface's IP configuration.
options.C: By naming its disk web-snet.
options.D: Through the public IP resource alone.

optionExplanations.A: The VM references the NIC, whose subnet_id points to web.
optionExplanations.B: Tags do not attach network interfaces.
optionExplanations.C: A disk name does not create network membership.
optionExplanations.D: The public IP provides an address; the NIC establishes subnet attachment.

questions.stem: Why does the introductory VM have a Standard public IP?

options.A: Because every Azure VM requires one.
options.B: To demonstrate intentional direct first access.
options.C: Because Terraform cannot use private IPs.
options.D: To automatically install IIS.

optionExplanations.A: Private-only VMs are supported.
optionExplanations.B: Later production guidance replaces public administration.
optionExplanations.C: The NIC also has a private IP.
optionExplanations.D: A public IP does not install software.

questions.stem: Where does admin_password obtain its configured value?

options.C: random_password.windows_admin.result
options.D: A fixed literal in terraform.tfvars.example.

optionExplanations.A: No password belongs in tags.
optionExplanations.B: Subscription identifiers are not passwords.
optionExplanations.C: Terraform generates the password rather than hardcoding it.
optionExplanations.D: The supplied compute resource references the random password result.

questions.stem: Why must the learner protect state for this VM even though its password output is sensitive?

options.A: The password is never persisted anywhere.
options.C: The public IP encrypts Terraform artifacts.
options.D: The generated password can still reside in state.

optionExplanations.A: The random result and VM configuration are tracked.
optionExplanations.B: It can include secret attributes too.
optionExplanations.C: Network addressing does not protect local files.
optionExplanations.D: Sensitive display redaction is not removal from stored state.

questions.stem: Which command explicitly reveals the sensitive Windows password and therefore belongs only in a private terminal?

options.C: terraform fmt -check
options.D: az account show --query id

optionExplanations.A: The raw named output can expose a marked-sensitive value.
optionExplanations.B: Ordinary output redacts marked-sensitive values.
optionExplanations.C: Formatting does not retrieve the credential.
optionExplanations.D: That reads subscription context.

questions.stem: Test-NetConnection to TCP 3389 succeeds. What does that prove by itself?

options.B: The tested TCP path is reachable from that source.
options.C: IIS serves HTTP on port 80.
options.D: The VM is backed up.

optionExplanations.A: No RDP credential login is tested.
optionExplanations.B: It does not prove successful Windows authentication.
optionExplanations.C: That is a different service and port.
optionExplanations.D: Connectivity does not verify backup.

questions.stem: RDP worked yesterday but fails after the learner changes home networks. What should be checked first?

options.A: Whether the saved /32 still equals the current NIC private address.
options.B: Whether the Lab tag is uppercase.
options.C: Whether the current public IPv4 matches admin_cidr.
options.D: Whether every inbound port is open.

optionExplanations.A: The direct administration source is the learner's public IPv4, not the VM NIC address.
optionExplanations.B: That does not select the traffic source.
optionExplanations.C: The rule is restricted to that source.
optionExplanations.D: Broad exposure is not the intended fix.

questions.stem: A VM create request fails with a regional family-quota error. Which response fits the lesson?

options.C: Use a broader RDP CIDR.
options.D: Choose an approved suitable size/region or resolve the quota first.

optionExplanations.A: That does not supply vCPU capacity.
optionExplanations.B: Credential display does not affect quota.
optionExplanations.C: Traffic exposure does not increase quota.
optionExplanations.D: Revisit the regional readiness checks.

questions.stem: The image version is latest. What production implication should be considered?

options.A: Future deployments may resolve to a newer image version.
options.B: Existing VMs automatically rebuild at every release.
options.C: latest means the VM has no OS.
options.D: It disables all Windows patching permanently.

optionExplanations.A: Production reproducibility may require a reviewed pinned image/version.
optionExplanations.B: Image selection does not imply that behavior.
optionExplanations.C: It selects an available image version.
optionExplanations.D: The reference does not establish a patch policy.

questions.stem: Which factor dominates CLZ-190's compute charges?

options.B: VM size and allocated running time.
options.C: The length of the Lab tag.
options.D: The number of VNet subnet labels.

optionExplanations.A: Documentation does not allocate compute.
optionExplanations.B: The chosen SKU and hours drive compute cost.
optionExplanations.C: Tags are not the dominant compute driver.
optionExplanations.D: Subnet naming does not drive allocated VM compute hours.

questions.stem: If the VM is deallocated but retained, which resource can still incur cost?

options.C: Its managed OS disk and retained public IP.
options.D: No retained Azure resource can cost anything.

optionExplanations.A: Markdown files do not allocate Azure disks.
optionExplanations.B: Local output files do not create Azure charges.
optionExplanations.C: Stopping compute does not delete those resources.
optionExplanations.D: Deallocation is not complete resource deletion.

questions.stem: Which command supplies the documented Azure power-state evidence?

options.C: terraform fmt
options.D: az vm list --resource-group $resourceGroup --show-details

optionExplanations.A: That checks configuration consistency.
optionExplanations.B: That evaluates metadata expressions.
optionExplanations.C: That formats source.
optionExplanations.D: The query reads deployed VM details.

sources.title: Create a Windows VM using Azure CLI

questions.stem: What private IP allocation mode is configured on the VM NIC?

options.B: Static public only, with no private address.
options.C: DHCP from the learner's home router.
options.D: A private address selected manually in the VM block.

optionExplanations.A: The NIC IP configuration declares Dynamic.
optionExplanations.B: The NIC also has a subnet private IP.
optionExplanations.C: The NIC is inside Azure's VNet.
optionExplanations.D: The NIC declaration requests dynamic private allocation.

questions.stem: Which public IP settings are supplied in CLZ-190?

options.C: Standard SKU with no address allocation.
options.D: An NSG-generated floating address.

optionExplanations.A: That is not the source declaration.
optionExplanations.B: Both are explicit in the public IP resource.
optionExplanations.C: Static allocation is declared.
optionExplanations.D: The address is a separate public IP resource.

questions.stem: Unlike CLZ-180's subnet association, where does CLZ-190 associate its web NSG?

options.C: The web network interface.
options.D: The generated password.

optionExplanations.A: NSGs do not attach to OS disks.
optionExplanations.B: The association is not tenant-wide.
optionExplanations.C: The source uses a NIC security-group association.
optionExplanations.D: A password is not a network association target.

questions.stem: Why should admin_cidr=198.51.100.0/24 fail this lesson's validator?

options.A: A /24 is not valid IPv4 CIDR syntax.
options.C: Every CIDR must equal the default example.
options.D: The prefix length must be 32.

optionExplanations.A: It is valid syntax but too broad here.
optionExplanations.B: It requires IPv4.
optionExplanations.C: The learner supplies their own matching /32.
optionExplanations.D: The source restricts the allowed shape to one IPv4 host.

questions.stem: A supplied IPv4 /32 passes validation. Which additional claim is unsafe?

options.A: That it is guaranteed public and reachable.
options.C: That IPv6-style colon notation is excluded.
options.D: That a supported input can be stored locally.

optionExplanations.A: The code checks syntax/prefix length, not public classification or reachability.
optionExplanations.B: That is checked.
optionExplanations.C: The validation checks that.
optionExplanations.D: The lesson uses local inputs.

questions.stem: Why does admin_username=Administrator fail the configured input validation?

options.C: Every username must be a subscription GUID.
options.D: The public IP must be Dynamic first.

optionExplanations.A: It contains no digits.
optionExplanations.B: lower() is checked against the disallowed list.
optionExplanations.C: Usernames and subscription IDs are distinct.
optionExplanations.D: Public IP allocation does not determine username validation.

questions.stem: vm_size matches Standard_[A-Za-z0-9_]+. What remains to be verified?

options.B: Whether it contains an underscore after Standard.
options.C: Actual regional availability and quota for that SKU.
options.D: Whether uppercase letters are allowed.

optionExplanations.A: The pattern checks that.
optionExplanations.B: The pattern checks that separator.
optionExplanations.C: The regex proves only a plausible string shape.
optionExplanations.D: The pattern explicitly permits letters of either case.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the VM's declared OS disk?

options.A: Store the Azure CLI's local login cache.
options.C: Replace the network interface.
options.D: Store the installed operating system on managed storage.

optionExplanations.A: That cache is on the workstation.
optionExplanations.B: A disk does not grant roles.
optionExplanations.C: Storage and networking are separate dependencies.
optionExplanations.D: Its storage tier contributes separate cost.

questions.stem: A learner collects screenshots for a public issue. Which content must be excluded?

options.C: The lesson identifier CLZ-190.
options.D: The Terraform command names.

optionExplanations.A: Troubleshooting evidence must not publish the credential.
optionExplanations.B: That can be useful diagnostic evidence.
optionExplanations.C: That is public curriculum metadata.
optionExplanations.D: Command names alone are not secrets.

questions.stem: Does the supplied CLZ-190 module install and validate IIS?

options.B: No; the IIS bootstrap is a subsequent lesson.
options.C: Yes; every Windows image serves HTTP by default.
options.D: Only if the VM name contains web.

optionExplanations.A: An NSG rule does not install features.
optionExplanations.B: This lesson establishes the Windows VM and first access.
optionExplanations.C: Do not assume that application behavior.
optionExplanations.D: Names do not install software.

sources.title: Create a Windows VM using Azure CLI

questions.stem: The local network blocks outbound TCP 3389. What is a sensible troubleshooting step?

options.C: Check local egress restrictions and use an approved access path.
options.D: Change only the VM's Lab tag.

optionExplanations.A: That cannot repair local outbound filtering.
optionExplanations.B: Output redaction does not affect TCP.
optionExplanations.C: The end-to-end path includes the learner's network.
optionExplanations.D: Tags do not control local egress.

questions.stem: Which change directly addresses the lesson's intentional public administration exception?

options.C: Store the password in a public tag.
options.D: Remove the VM public IP and use Bastion/private connectivity.

optionExplanations.A: Naming does not remove exposure.
optionExplanations.B: That broadens direct administration.
optionExplanations.C: That exposes a secret.
optionExplanations.D: It changes the management path deliberately.

questions.stem: The exercise changes vm_size. What should the learner inspect before applying?

options.A: Whether the plan proposes an in-place resize or replacement.
options.B: Assume every resize is guaranteed nondisruptive.
options.C: Delete the state file to avoid replacement.
options.D: Check only the new name's spelling.

optionExplanations.A: Review actual provider actions and constraints.
optionExplanations.B: Size changes can have consequences.
optionExplanations.C: That loses ownership bindings.
optionExplanations.D: Format alone is insufficient.

questions.stem: Which set describes resources this VM lesson adds beyond a bare resource group?

options.B: NIC, public IP, disk, network, NSG, and generated credential.
options.C: A Kubernetes cluster and SQL server.
options.D: A mandatory remote-state backend.

optionExplanations.A: Tags are attributes.
optionExplanations.B: These support networking, storage, and authentication.
optionExplanations.C: Neither is declared.
optionExplanations.D: This lesson does not add that backend.

sources.title: Create a Windows VM using Azure CLI

questions.stem: Why is deallocating the VM insufficient for the lesson's documented cleanup?

options.B: Deallocation deletes the resource group automatically.
options.C: It leaves retained resources and state instead of removing the lab.
options.D: Terraform state always disappears when Windows stops.

optionExplanations.A: It does not.
optionExplanations.B: It does not remove the group.
optionExplanations.C: The lab calls for Terraform destroy and Azure readback.
optionExplanations.D: Guest/compute state does not erase Terraform state.

questions.stem: After destroy, can historical state backups or saved plans still contain prior credentials?

options.A: No; Azure remotely wipes every workstation file.
options.B: Only if the password output was nonsensitive.
options.C: The raw password becomes public-safe immediately.
options.D: Yes; retained local artifacts need protection and appropriate cleanup.

optionExplanations.A: Azure does not control all local artifacts.
optionExplanations.B: Sensitive values can also persist in artifacts.
optionExplanations.C: Old credentials should still not be published.
optionExplanations.D: Deleting managed Azure resources does not sanitize every copy.

questions.stem: Which combination matches the lesson's broader production guidance?

options.A: Hardened images, managed identities, patching, backup, endpoint protection, and secret rotation.
options.B: Public RDP plus no backups or patching.
options.C: Only a longer VM name.
options.D: Disable monitoring to reduce every risk.

optionExplanations.A: First access is only one part of secure VM operations.
optionExplanations.B: That discards the stated operational controls.
optionExplanations.C: Naming does not provide operational protection.
optionExplanations.D: Visibility is part of responsible operations.
